extraction.name: LUMA
extraction.description: LUMA (Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal data) is a multimodal benchmark dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data. It includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages (~3 GB), extending CIFAR-10/100 with audio from three corpora and LLM-generated text. It enables controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty for each modality.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Fournier
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled from three modalities: (1) Images from CIFAR-10/100 datasets, supplemented with EDM diffusion-generated images; (2) Audio samples extracted from three audio corpora (Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, Mozilla Common Voice) using forced alignments, plus 73 voluntarily contributed recordings from colleagues; (3) Text passages generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct LLM with 13 different prompts per class label. Audio samples underwent automatic validation using OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model and manual validation via Label Studio with 17 annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Classes with fewer than 600 validated audio samples were excluded from in-distribution data and used as OOD samples instead. For image modality, EDM diffusion-generated images were added to supplement classes with insufficient samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from CIFAR-10/100 (32x32 images) and EDM-generated images; audio recordings from The Spoken Wikipedia (phoneme-level aligned), LibriSpeech (1,000 hours of English speech from audiobooks), and Mozilla Common Voice (crowdsourced voices); 73 additional voluntarily contributed audio recordings; text generated by Gemma-7B Instruct LLM using 13 prompts per class label.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual validation of audio samples using a binary yes/no task. Annotators were asked 'Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)' with answer options of 'Yes' or 'No'. Colleagues with advanced to fluent English knowledge were recruited. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 71.61% annotation agreement was achieved. Samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted (5,027 samples); samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators who are colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for automatic audio transcription validation; Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model for text generation
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently lacks dependent modalities, limiting comprehensive studies of uncertainty quantification and applicability in information retrieval contexts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and benchmarking models that learn from uncertain and multimodal data (image, audio, and text), supporting uncertainty quantification research and information retrieval.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is open-source and extensible; the authors plan to add dependent modalities and more data samples in the future, with community contributions facilitated through the open-source pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Multiple uncertainty injection mechanisms are provided: (1) Data diversity control via inverse-distance-weighted sampling using deep features (Wav2Vec for audio, BERT for text, VGG-11 for images) with a tunable parameter k; (2) Sample noise injection — background noise from ESC-50 for audio via audiomentations, various text noise types (keyboard, OCR, random character, antonym, random word, spelling, back-translation) via nlpaug, and 15 image perturbations (Gaussian noise, blur types, weather effects, etc.) following Hendrycks and Dietterich; (3) Label noise injection by reassigning labels based on nearest-neighbor distances in deep feature space; (4) OOD sample injection using held-out classes not present in training data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio samples were manually validated using Label Studio with 2 annotations per sample from 17 annotators; samples with 71.61% agreement (both annotators confirming validity) were accepted (5,027 samples); conflicting annotations were rejected. Classes with more than 600 validated samples were retained as in-distribution (42 classes), and 8 remaining classes were designated as OOD data. For baseline models, 128x128 mel-spectrograms were extracted from padded audio samples; BERT embeddings were extracted per token and averaged for text; deep features were extracted using Wav2Vec, BERT, and VGG-11 for diversity and label-noise computations.

name.evidence: We propose LUMA, a unique multimodal dataset, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset, extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora, and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we used three audio/text parallel corpora and extracted the desired audio segments. More specifically, we used The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice corpora... We utilized Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model to generate more than 1,200 texts samples per class

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: We took another 8 classes, which had less than 600 samples after aligning with other modalities, as OOD samples... we decided to sample 600 data points with different level of diversity from the bigger set CIFAR-10/100. However, in CIFAR-100 dataset, there are no more than 600 samples per class. We alleviated this issue with including images generated with EDM Diffusion-based generative model.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The dataset includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages, amounting to approximately 3 GB of data... we used The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice corpora... We utilized Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model to generate more than 1,200 texts samples per class, using 13 different prompts.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: In the future, we plan to include dependent modalities, enabling more comprehensive studies of uncertainty quantification as well as improved applicability in information retrieval contexts.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we propose LUMA, a multimodal dataset for learning from uncertain and multimodal data. The dataset spans image, audio, and text modalities, and is accompanied by a Python package that allows users to generate customized versions with varying levels and types of noise and uncertainty.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The dataset can be easily extended with additional modalities and augmented with more data samples... The open-source nature of the data compilation pipeline and code for uncertainty and noise generation facilitates the integration of new contributions from the community.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We prioritized flexibility, offering multiple options for controlling uncertainty through adjustable parameters such as data diversity, sample-level noise, label corruption, and the injection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples... For audio modality, we added background noise... from the ESC-50 dataset... For text modality, we utilize the nlpaug library... For image modality, we added different types of noise suggested and implemented by Hendrycks and Dietterich... we randomly select a subset of samples based on a user-defined probability... we kept a separate set of samples from the same dataset, but belonging to classes that are not present in the training data, as OOD samples.
